questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, it was inside Europe, which made the procedure easier compared to destinations outside Europe, as it was part of the Erasmus programme. Second, the city of Rome just stood out to me as an especially interesting and charming city, and I was very interested in going to Italy to explore its culture, history, way of living, nature etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall it was good, but the University was not close to being as good as KU. The courses where very messy in general, and the facilities such as good reading spots were not that good. Furthermore, the infrastructure in Rome is pretty bad, so you don't feel very flexible in Rome. Having said that, I still learned something new and also had to work hard. And as a place to explore, you will never get done with Rome. There is so much to do.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received several informing letters by e-mail, which was good. But I had a lot of confussion in the beginning about how to use different apps and platforms and where I could even see my schedule. And many Erasmus students including me had a lot of technical problems in the beginning, which was very frustrating.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some information letters, and I was invited by some tutors to different chats about the welcome week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It took some work, but it worked out. There are a lot of scammers, so the harderst part is to judge whether someone is fake or real.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find something relatively close to uni or buy a bike, because the public transport is so unreliable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think I received some mails from them with links to different platforms, where you could read about different courses and register. I only had one week or so from when I received the mail to actually decide on which courses to enroll in, and it was in the end of June, som it was quite stressfull, since I had a lot of other plans at that time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Different guides

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went fine, but it was almost impossible to get a good overview of which courses were overlapping each other. Their system for that was definitely very bad.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing special

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There was a great difference between the level in different courses. It depends very much on the professor. In general, the courses are differing more in form and level than I am used to in Denmark. I had two courses with a high level, and two with a low level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focus on active participation on Luiss, and they are registrating your presence. The style of teaching are much more unstructured and depends on how the professor likes to do it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geopolitics, technology and population
Diplomacy and negotiation
Crisis communication
Mediteranean history and culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will especially recommend diplomacy and negotiation. The professor was the former Italian ambassador in Algeria and was still and active diplomat. He had obviously a deep and practical knowledge and was highly skilled. Among other things, we had a simulation of a future peace conference in the Russia-Ukraine-conflict, and it worked out very well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I rented an electric bike for 3 months since the public transport was so unreliable and I was living 7,5 km from the uni. Unfortunately, I once dropped the battery on the road, and I ended up paying 435 euros to get it repaired :(

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books were less expensive, since all off the material was accesible online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There was different options, but it was kind of unaccesible since it required some medical tests to even enroll for some of the sport teams, and it was almost impossible to get a time at the doctor. 
Instead, I participated in a football tournament every week, but that was arranged by some tutors and not the uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different sports activities and some different cultural courses

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The football tournament was great fun and a good way of meeting other people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do trips to places like Napoli, Abruzzo, Viterbo, Firenze, Bologna and Perugia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, Italians are very relaxed

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Drink a lot of coffee outside, and ask random people after classes where they are going for lunch.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How messy and unstructured they are, both professors and students. Very bad communication in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their relaxed attitude and how much they are all into history, culture and food. They are good at not getting frustrated if something is not working or delayed or very chaotic.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Eat out a lot and experience as many museums and churches as possible
Do the diplomacy and negotiation course
Don't be frustrated, but accept that many things are not working as they are in Denmark

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know and great city as Rome very well

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Actually it was the transportation issue

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
